questions.prompt: Which directive must error.tsx start with, and why?

options.text: "use client" — it uses reset() and onClick, which need a Client Component
"use server" — error boundaries run only on the server
No directive — it's a plain Server Component

questions.explanation: error.tsx is interactive (reset, onClick), so it must be a Client Component and start with "use client".

questions.prompt: Which props does error.tsx receive? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: error.tsx receives the thrown error and a reset function; params/searchParams are page props, not error-boundary props.

questions.prompt: Which function (from next/navigation) triggers the not-found UI and a 404? Type its name.
questions.explanation: notFound() renders the nearest not-found.tsx and returns a 404 status.

questions.prompt: Which errors does a segment's error.tsx NOT catch?

options.text: Errors thrown in the root layout itself
Errors in a nested child component
Errors in a component it renders

questions.explanation: error.tsx covers its segment and below, but not the root layout. Root-layout errors need global-error.tsx (which renders its own <html>/<body>).

questions.prompt: Match each file or function to its role.
questions.explanation: error.tsx handles segment errors, not-found.tsx/notFound() handle 404s, and global-error.tsx handles root-layout failures.

questions.prompt: Order what happens when a component throws and the user retries.

items.text: A component in the segment throws during render
The nearest error.tsx renders with error and reset
The user clicks a button that calls reset()
The segment re-renders, attempting to recover

questions.explanation: The error boundary catches the throw and renders error.tsx; calling reset() re-renders the segment to recover.
